- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating upward momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overestimating downward pressure.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast growth to 5–7% per period post-spike.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.33 to -0.33), model often lags — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment reversal within 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after a peak), model often fails to recognize it — reduce forecast slope after peak by 10–15% for 3–5 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility — apply a 5–10% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33).  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals, model tends to smooth too much — allow 1–2% volatility in forecast for each reversal event.
